newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends down, trade, specs sell on close.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends down, trade, specs sell on close.

text.p: After remaining only slightly lower throughout most of the session, NYCE cotton futures racked up additional losses near the close to settle sharply lower.
Dealers said late-session trade and speculative selling took out stops around 75.10 basis March and pressured prices to the day's lows.
Today's weak settlement signals lower prices Thursday, traders said, pegging major support at 73.80 basis the most-active March contract.
March settled down 1.03 cent at 74.75 cents per pound, traded 75.75 to 74.70 cents. The back months finished 1.07 to 0.05 weaker.
Prices are expected to rise gradually based a bearish world supply and demand outlook.
"As we dip down into lower prices we will make more export sales and the market will rebound back up to 78.00," O.A. Cleveland, a cotton marketing specialist with Mississippi State University, said.
Players will be able to more accurately gauge the situation after the U.S. Department of Agriculture releases its monthly data on Thursday, Dec 12.
Open interest in the December contract stood at only 497 lots as of Tuesday. Friday is the final trading day for the contract.
